title: The Reuleaux Platonic Solids
description:
Version 3 adds Theorem 2: the largest width of the bodies on the dodecahedron, icosahedron, cube and octahedron is the face-axis width (Conjecture 1 proved for these four, by an exact case analysis of the boundary); Proposition 1: the corners of each of these bodies are exactly its face-axis points, one beyond each face of the solid; Corollary 4: dual pairs have the same width range; and the text revised for greater clarity.

This paper shows exactly how thin and how thick DICTO's Reuleaux Platonic solids are: thinnest across a diameter, thickest through a face. Put a ball on every corner of a Platonic solid of diameter 1, each of radius 1, and let B be what all the balls share (DICTO's idea). Main theorem: the smallest width of B is exactly 1, reached along any line through two corners at distance 1; and for the dodecahedron, icosahedron, cube and octahedron, with circumradius ½ and inradius r, the width along each axis through a face centre is exactly 2√(3/4 + r²) − 2r. Theorem 2: for these four this face-axis width is the largest width of B (Conjecture 1 of Versions 1 and 2, now proved by an exact case analysis of the boundary); on the way, the corners of B, where three or more spheres meet, are exactly its face-axis points (Proposition 1). Corollary: dual solids have the same ratio r/R, so dual pairs have exactly the same widths, from 1 up to (√(50 + 2√5) − √(5 + 2√5))/√15 ≈ 1.110989 for the balls on the dodecahedron and on the icosahedron and up to (√30 − √3)/3 ≈ 1.248392 for the balls on the cube and on the octahedron. The tetrahedron is the classical case, the Reuleaux tetrahedron, where the formula does not apply (its diameter is its edge, not twice its circumradius); its edge-midpoint axis gives √3 − √2/2 by the same argument, the value quoted as its largest width, and our volume agrees with the known closed form to 1.1 × 10−8. The four other bodies (not found in the sources checked) are not Reuleaux polyhedra in the sense of Montejano and Roldán-Pensado, following Sallee, or of Hynd. DICTO names the bodies by their look, the Reuleaux icosahedron (balls on the dodecahedron), dodecahedron (on the icosahedron), octahedron (on the cube) and cube (on the octahedron); each has the face pattern of the dual solid, and the fewest face colours, for the balls on the dodecahedron, icosahedron, cube, tetrahedron and octahedron, are 3, 4, 2, 4 and 3.

Finding #45 on dictospheres.com. Scripts, exact checks and data: https://github.com/DICTOR-Master/kaleidohedra/tree/f291ecbd/studies (research branch, commit f291ecbd: folders 2026-10-21-reuleaux-platonic and 2026-11-21-gaps-batch-c, item 2).

Version 2 (22 October 2026): adds a short opening explanation to each result, its proof and the conclusion. Version 1: 21 October 2026.
